output_parsed.paper_title: Present-day thermal and water activity environment of the Mars Sample Return collection

queries.query: For the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover at Jezero crater, use MEDA relative humidity (with respect to ice), surface pressure, air temperature, and TIRS 8–14 µm ground brightness temperature over the first Martian year to quantify the diurnal cycle of near-surface H2O volume mixing ratio and derive surface water activity constraints relevant to salt hydration and transient frost stability.

Using MEDA pressure and ambient air temperature measurements at the rover during Jezero crater operations, reconstruct the atmospheric state at rover sample-tube sealing events across sols spanning the first Martian year and estimate the corresponding sealed headspace water vapor partial pressure and inferred H2O abundance needed for sample-environment assessments.

output_parsed.paper_title: Present-day thermal and water activity environment of the Mars Sample Return collection

queries.query: For Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer observations, compile derived atmospheric column aerosol optical depths (dust and H2O ice) over Mars for seasonal context at northern mid‑latitudes near Jezero, using solar‑longitude binning comparable to 5° Ls climatology and focusing on daytime (~14:00 local time) sampling during Mars Years 24–27.

Using Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer atmospheric products, evaluate how the mission’s atmospheric recalibration affects derived column quantities relevant to near‑surface water vapor/opacity diagnostics by comparing recalibrated mapping‑phase observations across multiple seasons (binned by solar longitude) under daytime mid‑afternoon conditions.

output_parsed.paper_title: Present-day thermal and water activity environment of the Mars Sample Return collection

queries.query: For Mars 2020 Perseverance returned-sample activities in Jezero crater during the Delta Front campaign (roughly sols 415–707), identify the rover-generated documentation products that capture sampling acquisition context (abraded patch imaging/mineralogy/chemistry summaries, drilling/coring notes, and sealing event metadata) to reconstruct the operational and geologic setting of each sealed tube.

Using Mars 2020 Perseverance observations in Jezero crater during the Delta Front campaign (roughly sols 415–707), compile SHERLOC Raman/fluorescence detections from abrasion patches associated with sampling sites to evaluate the occurrence of hygroscopic salts (e.g., perchlorates/sulfates/chlorides) relevant to hydration–dehydration and potential near-surface water exchange processes.

final_output.query: For the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover at Jezero crater, use MEDA relative humidity (with respect to ice), surface pressure, air temperature, and TIRS 8–14 µm ground brightness temperature over the first Martian year to quantify the diurnal cycle of near-surface H2O volume mixing ratio and derive surface water activity constraints relevant to salt hydration and transient frost stability.

Using MEDA pressure and ambient air temperature measurements at the rover during Jezero crater operations, reconstruct the atmospheric state at rover sample-tube sealing events across sols spanning the first Martian year and estimate the corresponding sealed headspace water vapor partial pressure and inferred H2O abundance needed for sample-environment assessments.

For Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer observations, compile derived atmospheric column aerosol optical depths (dust and H2O ice) over Mars for seasonal context at northern mid‑latitudes near Jezero, using solar‑longitude binning comparable to 5° Ls climatology and focusing on daytime (~14:00 local time) sampling during Mars Years 24–27.

Using Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer atmospheric products, evaluate how the mission’s atmospheric recalibration affects derived column quantities relevant to near‑surface water vapor/opacity diagnostics by comparing recalibrated mapping‑phase observations across multiple seasons (binned by solar longitude) under daytime mid‑afternoon conditions.

For Mars 2020 Perseverance rover operations in Jezero crater during the crater-floor campaign (landing through ~sol 380), identify the returned-sample science documentation reports that summarize coring/abrasion activities and the associated PIXL, SHERLOC, and SuperCam observations used to interpret sulfate/chloride/perchlorate occurrence at sampling sites.

For Mars 2020 Perseverance returned-sample activities at Jezero crater, retrieve the mission returned-sample documentation archive that compiles per-sample acquisition provenance (tube handling, sealing context, and rover ancillary metadata) needed to reconstruct the environmental context of sample collection and caching.

For Mars 2020 Perseverance returned-sample activities in Jezero crater during the Delta Front campaign (roughly sols 415–707), identify the rover-generated documentation products that capture sampling acquisition context (abraded patch imaging/mineralogy/chemistry summaries, drilling/coring notes, and sealing event metadata) to reconstruct the operational and geologic setting of each sealed tube.

Using Mars 2020 Perseverance observations in Jezero crater during the Delta Front campaign (roughly sols 415–707), compile SHERLOC Raman/fluorescence detections from abrasion patches associated with sampling sites to evaluate the occurrence of hygroscopic salts (e.g., perchlorates/sulfates/chlorides) relevant to hydration–dehydration and potential near-surface water exchange processes.
